correctness.rationale: The normalized STFT reduces the signed fixed-pair contrast to g(t) against planar area, with shell measure dt for t=πr². The sign threshold is the geometric mean of n+1,…,m. On the positive branch, (log g)″ is strictly negative even at n=0, and the difference log g(a)−log g(a+A) increases from −∞ to A. Its zero yields a positive-level superlevel set of area A; integrating the signed deviations from that level proves uniqueness among arbitrary measurable sets. For k=1 the derivative equation on the positive branch is (t−(n+1))²=n+1. At both boundary circles the inside/outside cost sublevel area is (1/p+1/q)y+O(y²); thresholds attaining these small masses exist as collars, and the layer-cake inequality gives the same lower bound for nonradial removal and addition. With exchanged mass ε/2 on each side the total leading cost is ε²/[4(1/p+1/q)], so both the factor four and the harmonic combination are needed. For the proportional gap, compact Stirling expansions yield √N times g converging to the difference of two shifted normal densities. For fixed k the factorial ratio is 1+ku/√N+O(N⁻¹) on compacts, yielding (N/k)g→uφ(u). For either strictly log-concave positive limit the log-height difference at separation s has a simple unique zero. Its two-sided bracket lies inside the prelimit positive branch by local uniform convergence and brackets the prelimit zero by monotonicity. Integrating over the converging finite interval proves the two contrast limits.
residual_risks: In the Finding, ‘squared radii’ a,a+A means scaled squared radii t=πr²; literal Euclidean squared radii are a/π and (a+A)/π as given by the explicit set and area convention. This terminology does not alter the defined optimizer.
The stability expansion is for fixed n,m,A. It does not give uniform constants in the high-degree regimes; those limits have separate proofs.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct contribution is the combination of an exact all-mask, fixed ordered pair optimizer with its sharp local symmetric-difference constant and the optimized crossover (especially fixed k). The individual Gamma/Bargmann response, superlevel-set principle, and leading Gaussian profiles are not new. The closest prior critical-width annulus result supplies the proportional-gap contrast for any fixed scaled radial window by subtraction, but it neither selects the unique optimal window for a labelled signed pair among all masks nor gives the sharp coefficient or the fixed-gap optimized limit. No inspected source covers the distinct conclusion.
residual_risks: The primary lookup was bounded; unrelated hits and no exact catalogue hit do not certify priority. A general signed two-density measure-optimization result not indexed under STFT or localization could still overlap.

value.rationale: This asks a natural inverse mask-design question not answered by maximizing a single eigenvalue. The signed pair has a provable unique annulus for every positive area and a sharp all-competitor deficit revealing how optimally exchanged mass splits across two boundaries. Optimized fixed and √n gap regimes distinguish vanishing from nonvanishing contrast with explicit endpoints and constants. The useful content is not a re-evaluation of a single known annular eigenvalue.
residual_risks: No claim of operational quantum-discrimination optimality, arbitrary-window optimality, or a result uniform over intermediate scale regimes is justified.
